title: Fuzzy template-match validator and golden-sample harness for tokenizer onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: During model onboarding we've seen intermittent template mismatches caused by subtle tokenizer differences (subtoken splits, unicode normalizations, and role delimiter variants). These mismatches surface as coherent-but-incompatible chat envelopes that break downstream structured output parsing or cause token accounting regressions for customers pinned to a model version.

Goal: Implement a lightweight fuzzy-matching validator and a deterministic golden-sample harness that runs as part of onboarding pipelines and profile publishing. The validator should catch likely incompatibilities (e.g., >X% token alignment drift, role delimiter mismatches, or repeated subtoken boundary shifts) and classify them into soft warnings vs. hard gating failures. The golden-sample harness will keep a small curated set of prompts+expected-tokenization footprints per model variant to detect regressions across tokenizer/runtime changes.

Why fuzzy matching: Exact equality is brittle across minor normalization differences that don't affect semantics. Fuzzy heuristics (Levenshtein on token ids, role-aware anchors, and normalized whitespace collapse) let us escalate only real compatibility risks. This reduces onboarding friction while maintaining safety for pinned rollouts.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict gating (exact token equality) would block benign upgrades frequently; we prefer thresholded alerts and progressive enforcement.
- Heavier ML-based similarity models were rejected for now because they increase onboarding latency and add maintenance burden; heuristics plus golden-sample baseline are sufficient for initial coverage.
- Storing golden samples increases metadata surface area for bundles; we limit sample set to <= 20 per model variant and compress token footprints to reduce storage and privacy concerns.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Define token-footprint format: role markers, token ids, tokenized text preview, normalized whitespace hash, and a compact checksum.
2) Build fuzzy score functions: token-id Levenshtein ratio, role-anchor alignment score, and subtoken drift metric.
3) Integrate validator into onboarding pipeline: run against onboarding tokenizer output and compare to expected profile; produce structured result with severity and suggested remediation.
4) Create golden-sample harness: stored per-model JSONL, executed in CI and during runtime profile publishing with delta reporting in the console dashboard.
5) Add telemetry and SLOs: false-positive rate target <3% on sampled historical onboards, and detect noisy signal sources for future tuning.

Stakeholders: PM (Maya Zheng), Runtime lead (Noah Ramirez), DX (Evelyn Cho), Security reviewer (ops-security@redwood.com).

Artifacts and links: see links field for PRs, design doc, and console dashboard queries.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Validator runs automatically in onboarding pipeline and emits a human-readable report for each model variant.
2) Golden-sample harness stores and retrieves up to 20 samples per variant and produces pass/fail + delta metrics.
3) Console displays token-alignment drift and role-delimiter mismatch counts in a per-model profile page.
4) Onboard gating policy: soft warnings for fuzzy_score >= 0.8 and hard-gate when fuzzy_score < 0.6 with role-anchor mismatch OR subtoken drift > 12%.
5) False-positive rate measured on retrospective testset < 3%.
steps:
- Draft token-footprint schema and get design sign-off from Runtime and DX.
- Implement fuzzy scoring functions in serving-runtime utils (feature-flagged).
- Add golden-sample storage to model-bundles metadata and migration tool for existing profiles.
- Wire validator into onboarding pipeline; emit webhook events for Console and write to onboarding logs.
- Create CI job to run harness on nightly builds and block profile publish on hard-gate failures.
- Instrument telemetry and build dashboard panels for triage.
notes:
Recent incidents: ENG-87234 highlighted a fingerprint-guardrails issue where token boundary shifts during a runtime patch caused a canary failure. Post-mortem suggested adding deterministic sample checks. We reused some sample prompts from ENG-545321 and anonymized them.

Design feedback from DX: prefer displaying token diffs side-by-side with role anchors highlighted; storage of token ids should be optional and gated by customer privacy settings for private deployments.

Engineering constraints: keep runtime overhead of validator <50ms per onboarding sample by using compiled C++ Levenshtein or optimized Rust bindings; fall back to Python scoring in CI.
